patch_description: The original uses single-path greedy with random sampling (GRASP-like) but evaluates full-sequence costs and commits to one path, easily falling into local optima. I propose a hybrid: (1) a beam search that maintains multiple promising partial schedules, selecting each next transaction by actual incremental makespan cost (via workload.get_opt_seq_cost on partial sequences), pruning to a beam width; (2) GRASP-style randomized restarts with greedy-random candidate pools (choose among top-k near-min candidates) to diversify; (3) a final improvement pass doing adjacent-swap local search on the best schedule found, since swapping adjacent conflicting transactions can directly reduce conflict delay without full re-evaluation. Evaluating true makespan of partial sequences at each step grounds the heuristic in actual objective rather than proxies like txn length.
